summary: Canadian Geographic (Sep 2024) describes a 1927 two-storey lookout on Sinkut Mountain, staffed in fire season for the BC Wildfire Service; no later record of its fate was found.

facts.design: Two-storey building with windows on all sides of the top floor and a wraparound balcony

staffing.status: Staffed in fire season by one lookout for the BC Wildfire Service

access.note: A public road can reach the lookout, per the 2024 article. No source describes whether visitors may enter the building or pass the gate.

events.note: Canadian Geographic states the lookout was built in 1927.
Fire-season lookout Bart Vanderlinde, described as the last regular fire lookout in British Columbia, works stints of about 14 days at a time.

corrections.why: The provincial names database and the 2024 Canadian Geographic article both use Sinkut. The brief's Tsinkut spelling appears in no page I could open.

notes_for_editor: One substantial 2024 magazine feature carries the build date, design, staffing and road note; the map and names records confirm the location and tower type. The brief's local unit (Regional District of Bulkley-Nechako) is not confirmed by any page I read, so the story omits it. The CBC staffing article timed out twice and was not read. Facebook group pages are login walls, and AllTrails returned 403; neither is cited. Search snippets (not quoted) gave a distance of 23 km from Vanderhoof (CBC) and a 1930 replacement of a 1927 structure (a Facebook group post); both are unverified and kept out of the story. Access is set to restricted because the road is public but the building is a working station and no source confirms visitor entry. Read budget: about 9 fetch attempts (several failed or login-walled) and 2 searches.
